title: A Review of Time Series Prediction Models Based on Deep Learning
authors: Ao, X.; Gong, Y.; He, A.
tldr: A systematic review of DL-based time series prediction models covering classical architectures (MLP, CNN, RNN, Transformer) and emerging approaches (GNN, diffusion, state-space models), including benchmarks on financial and weather datasets and an analysis of limitations such as noise and distribution shifts.
problem_and_motivation: Existing reviews provide only partial coverage of deep learning for time series prediction, often restricted to single architecture families or lacking up-to-date coverage of emerging methods like diffusion models, state-space models, and large language model adaptations. A comprehensive survey is needed to support researchers working on non-stationary data characteristics common in real-world financial, energy, and weather time series.
approach: Proposed a hierarchical taxonomy of deep learning time series prediction methods based on structural and mathematical properties: MLP variants, CNN variants, RNN variants, Transformer variants, GNN variants, generative and hybrid models, and state-space models.
Summarized commonly used benchmark datasets across domains including finance (S&P 500, Yahoo Finance, NASDAQ), traffic, weather, energy (ETTh), electricity, and COVID-19.
Analyzed common evaluation metrics: MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and MSE across benchmarked studies.
Reviewed denoising methods, data preprocessing techniques, and patching strategies for handling noisy time series.
Discussed limitations and future directions including multimodal integration, LLM adaptation, and long-term sequence modeling.
findings: Transformer-based models (PatchTST, iTransformer) and hybrid CNN-Transformer architectures (TSMixer, TimesNet) consistently achieve top performance across multivariate long- and short-term time series prediction tasks.
GNN-based models excel at modeling spatial-temporal dependencies for multi-location weather prediction (e.g., GraphCast outperforms Google DeepMind for medium-range weather forecasting).
Diffusion-based models such as TimeGrad and SSSD effectively handle non-stationary distribution shifts and capture complex temporal dynamics via stochastic sampling.
State-space models like Mamba achieve linear time complexity while maintaining competitive performance with Transformers on long sequence modeling.
Data distribution shifts and poor data quality remain the most significant challenges for time series forecasting accuracy.

key_equations.explanation: General notation for time series prediction where the model maps historical covariates to future predictions.
Scaled dot-product attention mechanism central to Transformer-based time series models.
Measures linear correlation between two time series at different time lags to capture cross-variable dependencies.

definitions.definition: A single variable measured and recorded sequentially over time.
Multiple variables measured simultaneously, requiring modeling of both temporal and cross-variable dependencies.
A time series whose statistical properties (mean, variance, autocovariance) remain constant over time.
A contiguous subsequence extracted from the time series as a token for Transformer input, capturing local semantic patterns.
A condition where the statistical characteristics of a time series change over time, making prediction more difficult.
A generative model that progressively adds Gaussian noise to training data then learns to reverse the process for probabilistic forecasting.
A neural network framework modeling state evolution over time using linear recurrences, enabling efficient long-sequence modeling with linear time complexity.
A neural network operating on graph-structured data that learns both node representations and inter-node relationships for spatial-temporal forecasting.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides the most comprehensive taxonomy of deep learning time series prediction methods to date, covering eight architectural categories from classical MLP to emerging state-space models and LLM adaptations. Its key contributions include: (1) a structured hierarchical classification based on structural and mathematical properties rather than chronological or task-based categories; (2) benchmark performance analysis across financial, weather, and energy datasets with standardized evaluation metrics; and (3) identification of critical open problems including data distribution shifts, noise sensitivity, and the need for multimodal integration in future models.
directly_justifies: Deep learning models, especially Transformer-based and hybrid architectures, consistently outperform conventional methods for time series prediction across financial and energy domains.
Diffusion-based models effectively address non-stationary distribution shifts, a critical challenge in financial time series forecasting.
State-space models offer linear complexity competitive with Transformer performance for long sequence modeling.
Multimodal data integration and LLM adaptation represent emerging frontiers for improving time series forecasting.
limits: Focuses primarily on general time series benchmarks rather than personal finance-specific datasets.
Limited discussion of real-world deployment constraints such as computational costs and latency requirements.
Does not address user-facing explainability requirements for financial applications.
Excludes several Transformer variants (TSMixer, TimesNet) from detailed discussion despite acknowledging their strong performance.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: The systematic topic scan identified domain 6 (Predictive Modeling and Forecasting) as high relevance due to the paper's direct coverage of deep learning financial time series forecasting models including LSTM, Transformer, and diffusion architectures. Domain 5 (Anomaly Detection) received medium relevance for covering GNN and Transformer-based anomaly detection methods applicable to spending pattern anomalies. Domain 8 (Real-time Analytics) received low relevance for mentioning real-time processing limitations. Domains 1-4, 7, 9-14 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address financial behavior patterns, budgeting strategies, user profiling, mobile UX, or gamification. The paper's primary contribution is methodological rather than domain-specific to personal finance.

limitations: The survey excludes several Transformer variants such as TSMixer, TimesNet, and DLinear despite their strong benchmark performance.
Computational complexity and deployment requirements are not analyzed for the reviewed models.
Financial time series datasets are mentioned in benchmarks but not evaluated separately from other domains.
The discussion of denoising methods does not cover denoising score matching in sufficient depth for financial applications.
remember_this: Transformer-based models (PatchTST, iTransformer) and CNN-Transformer hybrids (TimesNet, TSMixer) consistently achieve top benchmark performance for time series prediction.
Diffusion models effectively handle non-stationary distribution shifts, making them particularly suitable for financial time series forecasting.
State-space models (Mamba, S4) offer linear time complexity competitive with Transformers for long sequence modeling, enabling efficient real-time applications.
Data quality and distribution shifts remain the primary challenges affecting forecasting accuracy across all reviewed architectures.
LLM adaptation for time series is an emerging frontier with potential to improve financial prediction through natural language context integration.
